Contributing to timesift

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Bug reports and pull requests are welcome on the issue tracker. With a bug report, include a small example that reproduces it.

Building and testing

The R package sits at the repository root, and so does the Python project: pyproject.toml and CMakeLists.txt build the Python extension from the same src/ the R package compiles. A Python source distribution cannot reach above its own project directory, so the project directory is the repository and there is one copy of the sources.

R, from the repository root:

devtools::test()

Python, from the repository root:

pip install -e ".[test,torch]"
pytest

The shared fixtures

inst/spec/representation.md describes what both languages compute, and inst/spec/fixtures/ holds a small input and the expected digests of every grain and statistic, plus the reference fits of the learners. Both test suites read the same fixtures.

  • A digest mismatch is a bug, never a fixture to regenerate. Fixtures are regenerated on the R side with inst/spec/make_fixtures.R, in a commit of their own, and only when the spec changes with them.
  • The test oracles are written from the spec. tests/testthat/helper-oracle.R and python/tests/oracle.py are pure-R and pure-NumPy implementations of the representation, used only by the suites. The NumPy one was written from the spec rather than from the R source, so the shared C++ core is checked against code that shares none of its own.
